title: Cambridge debenture and fall election-year borrowing authority
subtitle: Short special meeting also received the regional debenture issue report and passed routine by-laws.
overview: Regional Council met briefly in a special meeting to deal with debentures, which are long-term borrowing instruments. Council received a staff report on the regional debenture issue, which finances capital works in the City of Cambridge. It then passed a by-law authorizing $30,600,000 in twenty-year instalment debentures for Cambridge. Staff told council there is no new budget impact for the Region on this issue, as the debt servicing is paid by Cambridge.

Council also approved a by-law delegating authority to the outgoing council to pass debenture by-laws for the Region and its lower-tier municipalities {{vote:m1}}. 2026 is an election year, and the Municipal Act restricts council's ability to authorize financial liabilities between nomination day and the start of the new term. Staff said the delegation lets the Region and local municipalities borrow in the fall at a suitable time, taking market conditions into account.
For residents, the decisions keep Cambridge's capital financing on track and avoid a gap in borrowing ability during the election period. The meeting adjourned at 9:10 a.m.

decisions.detail: Council enacted a by-law authorizing twenty-year instalment debentures totalling $30,600,000 for capital works of the City of Cambridge.
Council enacted a by-law delegating authority to the outgoing council to pass debenture by-laws for the Region and its lower-tier municipalities during the election-year restriction period.

debate: Staff said the delegation by-law is needed because the Municipal Act limits council's ability to authorize financial liabilities between nomination day and the start of the new term in an election year.
Staff argued the delegation preserves flexibility for the Region and participating lower-tier municipalities to access long-term financing at the right time, based on market conditions.

One councillor asked whether council had delegated this authority before, recalling delegation to the chief administrative officer in a lame-duck situation. Staff replied that this is the same process used in past election years.
Staff noted the delegation approach is supported by the Region's external legal counsel, whose opinion is required in the debenture process.
